paper.title_en: Improving the signal-to-noise ratio through postselection of coincident detections in anticounterfeiting and quantum key distribution
paper.abstract_en: In quantum communications and other photon-counting applications, reliably detecting weak optical signals against a strong noise background remains a fundamental challenge. In this paper, we develop a simple idea: when a signal is carried by pairs (or more generally multiplets) of photons emitted simultaneously, postselection of coincident detections recorded on two detectors makes it possible to improve-sometimes drastically-the Signal to Noise Ratio. Essentially, this is made possible by the fact that genuine and accidental coincidences scale differently with the width of the postselection window. As long as the window remains wide enough to retain detections from the same pair, the genuine coincidence rate is approximately unchanged. In contrast, coincidences formed from independent clicks decrease linearly as the window is narrowed. The resulting signal-to-noise ratio, therefore, increases inversely with the window width. Our approach makes it possible to reveal photon-pair signals that are otherwise hidden beneath a much stronger uncorrelated background. We analyze here applications of this idea to quantum key distribution, metrology, and anti-counterfeiting.
